title: The best of times is happening at @New York City Center. 🌈 Nearly 45 ...
transcript: New York City center always seems to bring the right show at the right moment. But nothing has ever felt more perfectly timed than LA Cage aux Folles returning to New York City during Pride Month. As soon as LA Cage was announced last year, I made my friend Nicole Promise she'd come with me. After all, she does have a Zaza tattoo. We started the evening off editing incredible queer bar in the city called rise, where I Learned that so many of my friends had never seen LA Cage aux Folles before, but I just knew they would fall completely in love with it. This is a musical by Jerry Herman and Harvey Fierstein, based on a French play of the same name. If you've seen the movie The Birdcage, it's also inspired by the same material. It's about longtime partners George and Alban, who run a glamorous drag night club in France, and their son is getting married to a girl from an ultra conservative family. It forces them all to navigate questions of identity and acceptance and love and what it means to be yourself in a world that doesn't always feel like it has space for you. The musical was written in 1983, but unfortunately it is still extremely relevant. The New York City Center Encores! Production is directed by Robert O'hara. It's modernized, but still honours everything that makes LA Cage feel like such a classic and features an all black seeing this show through a black lens. Adds so much to the story and its themes and is ultimately a Celebration of queer black joy and love and community and family. And we don't get to see enough of that on stage. And truly, the heart of this show is Wayne Brady and Billy Porter. They are so perfectly cast. Their chemistry is effortless. It feels like they've been in love for decades. And the moment I will remember forever is Billy Porter singing I am what I am. Everyone was completely destroyed. Encore shows are technically concert versions, but this one goes all out. Incredible choreography and some of the most stunning costumes and wigs I've ever seen. And then, of course, the star of all city centre shows the score. They use the original 1983 orchestrations with a 28 piece orchestra. It feels so full. You just have to hear it live. At a time where queer families continue to face attacks, there is something incredibly powerful about sitting in a theater full of people cheering and crying and celebrating this story together. Lacaj has always been about living authentically and loving boldly, and right now this message hits especially hard. Go experience the best of times at New York City Center through June 28th and happy pride!
classificationReason: Full first-hand review of La Cage at NYCC Encores with clear personal attendance, plot overview, and strong opinions about the production's relevance and emotional impact.
